problem_text:
A logistics manager is assembling a shipment of specialized components to maximize total utility while adhering to a cargo weight limit.

The components available are:
* Component A: weight 34kg, utility 249 units
* Component B: weight 28kg, utility 113 units
* Component C: weight 26kg, utility 41 units
* Component D: weight 23kg, utility 267 units
* Component E: weight 25kg, utility 244 units
* Component F: weight 37kg, utility 216 units
* Component G: weight 37kg, utility 139 units
* Component H: weight 39kg, utility 66 units
* Component I: weight 41kg, utility 98 units
* Component J: weight 19kg, utility 97 units
* Component K: weight 41kg, utility 292 units
* Component L: weight 49kg, utility 286 units
* Component M: weight 26kg, utility 141 units
* Component N: weight 9kg, utility 51 units
* Component O: weight 20kg, utility 232 units
* Component P: weight 20kg, utility 232 units
* Component Q: weight 40kg, utility 11 units
* Component R: weight 32kg, utility 114 units
* Component S: weight 34kg, utility 155 units
* Component T: weight 13kg, utility 16 units
* Component U: weight 49kg, utility 273 units
* Component V: weight 20kg, utility 59 units
* Component W: weight 27kg, utility 195 units
* Component X: weight 47kg, utility 205 units
* Component Y: weight 24kg, utility 205 units
* Component Z: weight 14kg, utility 170 units
* Component AA: weight 1kg, utility 40 units
* Component BB: weight 7kg, utility 267 units

Furthermore, due to compatibility requirements, exactly one of Component A and Component B must be included.

If Component C is included, it necessitates special handling equipment that reduces the effective cargo capacity by 10 kg.
The transport vehicle can carry a maximum of 547 kg. The manager must determine which components to include in the shipment.
